title: Late Breaking Results: On the One-Key Premise of Logic Locking
problem: Logic locking security evaluation assumes only one correct key can unlock protected circuits. This work demonstrates that multiple incorrect key combinations can also produce correct functionality, invalidating the one-key security premise underlying conventional logic locking techniques.
motivation: Logic locking is a critical hardware security technique for protecting circuit intellectual property; understanding its fundamental vulnerabilities enables better protection mechanisms.
method: The attack searches for multiple potentially incorrect keys that collectively produce correct circuit functionality instead of finding the single correct key. Key-search tasks are parallelized across multi-core environments to exploit the availability of multiple valid key combinations.
key_novelty: Challenges the one-key premise by exploiting the existence of multiple valid key combinations and demonstrating this enables parallelizable attacks with dramatic speedup.
contributions: Challenges the fundamental one-key assumption underlying logic locking security evaluation
Proposes a parallelizable multi-key attack methodology exploiting multiple valid key combinations
Demonstrates 99.6% runtime reduction compared to conventional single-key attacks
Reveals critical vulnerability in logic locking evaluation assumptions
limitations: Paper does not discuss practical defenses against multi-key attacks or limitations of the proposed methodology.
primary_theme: breaking logic locking via multi-key parallelizable attack
